steps.text: Place sour cream and buttermilk into a mixing bowl. Season with parsley, chives, garlic powder, dill, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Whisk together until smooth. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: No-Mayonnaise Ranch Dressing
raw_recipe.description: If you do not like mayonnaise, this recipe is for you! It's so creamy, you'll never be able to tell that it's reduced fat! Couldn't be easier!
raw_recipe.name: No-Mayonnaise Ranch Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Place sour cream and buttermilk into a mixing bowl. Season with parsley, chives, garlic powder, dill, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Whisk together until smooth. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous dressing! It's great to find a buttermilk ranch dressing that doesn't contain mayo! Even though I like mayo this was a really refreshing change especially if you're looking to cut fat and calories. I used low-fat buttermilk and a light sour cream. I upped the dill a bit and used fresh chives instead of dried. I added a bit of sugar to taste and it as perfect for salads and as a veggie dip!
Love it.! So glad to find dressing with no Mayonnaise. I did add a little more seasoning than called for and added a tbsp lemon juice and 2 tbsp of olive oil. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

While creamy and free of corn, gluten, and soy (hello new allergies), this had zero flavor. I ended up needing 4 teaspoons dill weed, 3 teaspoons parsley and chives, 2 teaspoons garlic and onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt and a little over 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper. I also added a pinch of smoked paprika. Now it tastes like my previous homemade mayo based ranch dressing.

To us, this is a good & quick sub. I'm thinking of adding more of the same spices. It's almost too cream-y tasting. I sinned & added some mayo. What I tried & will add to: 3/4c each sour cream & mayo; 1/4c buttermilk; 1/2t parsley; outta chives; 1/4t each granulated garlic (1/2 = 4 cloves), dill, onion powder, salt; 1/8t pepper - & 2t apple cider vinegar. It's a little thin, but not runny. 'Glad I tried...A few days later: Much more like the real deal! Day one: eh (as expected) Day two: kinda like storebrand Then on: Mmmm! Like it. I didn't add more spices as I threatened to. It just improved drastically with time.

With some modifications, was great. We can't have buttermilk, so I just used sour cream. I did add some Apple Cider Vinegar and Lemon Juice to give it the zip it was missing from us not using buttermilk. Also, found that I had to double the seasonings. My husband and 8 year old daughter also think this dressing is great.

This dressing is excellent, I just added 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 1 packet of stevia. It is essential to let this sit in the fridge for several hours. Thanks so much for sharing a healthy / preservative free dressing!

Yummy! We do like Mayo, but I wanted to do a healthier alternative. I actually use 1 cup fat free plain yogurt, and 1/3 cup Light Sour Cream, and 1/3 cup Veganaise grapeseed oil Mayo. (sometimes a splash of buttermilk too) I'm sure it would be great as written though, and the spices are just perfect! My husband likes a thick dressing and LOTS of it. He is also so picky about his Ranch (he was attached to the bottled stuff) But he absolutely LOVES this. He eats it every day at lunch on his Salads. I did NOT want to be feeding him MSG and tons of fat and preservatives everyday, so this recipe is a Lifesaver!
I made a dairy free version of this recipe due to food allergies. I used canned coconut milk and a few drops of lemon juice. It was just great.
so good! i normally add more dill, basically double the amount

I'm on a special diet that limits sugar and carbs for a short period of time. I'll be eating a lot of salad and COULD NOT find a rand dressing without sugar, sucralose, dextrose, maltodextrin, etc... The buttermilk did have some sugar in it but wasn't as bad as store brands. So I only used 1/4th of a cup and ended up with a creamier dressing. I love chives so I doubled up on those and added a bit more onion powder. I love bold flavors. I tried it when first made on some cucumber slices. My sister, who loathes ranch tried it and literally licked the bowl (she's 20 years old) so that says something amazing about this dressing. I also made some great buffalo wings and this was amazing! Even better after sitting in the fridge for awhile. Thanks for the recipe. I'll be making it weekly, even after this diet is over!

Alright... good substitute when in a pinch. However it is vital to let sit in fridge for an hour or so. Any less and certain ingredients stand out... longer you chill, the better the flavors blend into one taste. very yummy after that:)
Great with some extra garlic & onion powder
I messed up and had to doctor. We're going to try again.
Delicious!!!!tastes like hidden Valley Ranch I'll never buy it again
Due to allergies and dislike to mayo. I really wanted a salad dressing and didn’t like the taste of olive oil in some dressings. So I was soooo happy I found this recipe . Love the taste of it !
Very good substitute for store bought ranch with soy in it which I'm allergic to.
My kids like ranch with their veggies, and this is a great alternative to a big bottle of soybean oil. It's thick enough to use as a dip or a dressing.
Love it. The egg in the mayo is too strong for me in the other recipe.
